findings.title: Legacy upgrade path drops an exchange-reported abort that arrives after upgrading.set(true) but before the 101 (onOpen)
findings.description: 184e89c sets `upgrading` before upgrades.run, i.e. before decodeQuery, the Origin check (403), registry.reserve (503) and ex.webSocket. Any HttpExchange.onAbort notification in that window is ignored even though no upgrade has happened yet. When ex.webSocket reports the abort and throws before onOpen, the IOException goes to errors.handle, which commits a 500 on the still-NEW response: the response ends COMPLETED, no res.onAbort listener runs, and the access log writes `GET /ws 500 ... ` without `aborted`. This violates FR-HTTP-035 AC-7 (an exchange-reported abort runs each listener once) and makes the FR-APP-019 line misreport the request. Built-in TinyHttpd masks it only because its commit after its own abort throws (checkNotAborted), which then aborts the response (contrast test passes); an adapter that accepts the error commit, like the RecordingExchange fixture the existing AC-7 legacy test uses, shows the defect. The same window covers the 403 Origin and 503 reserve error responses.

findings.suggested_fix: Stop ignoring the hook from the moment the session is open, not from before upgrades.run: e.g. flip the flag from the session's onOpen (DefaultWebSocketSession.opened()) or pass a callback into WebSocketUpgrade.upgrade that sets it once onOpen ran, so pre-onOpen aborts still call res.abort(null) (then errors.handle/afterFailure is a no-op on an ABORTED response and the line is marked aborted). Add the proof test as a regression test in ResponseOnAbortTest.

findings.title: Check-then-act race between res.state()==NEW and upgrading.set(true) can start an upgrade on an ABORTED response
findings.description: The request thread reads res.state()==NEW, then sets upgrading, then calls upgrades.run. An adapter-thread abort landing between the state read and the flag set aborts the response (onDone writes a `GET /ws 200 ... aborted` line) while the request thread still calls ex.webSocket; a permissive exchange would then open a session and its handshake line, giving two GET /ws lines, and res.upgraded() is a no-op. Deciding NEW->upgrading under the response lock would close it. Not proven: there is no exchange call between the check and the set to inject the abort deterministically, and built-in TinyHttpd refuses webSocket after its abort.

evidence.command: static analysis only (no deterministic injection point between Dispatcher.java:337 and :339)

findings.suggested_fix: Make the NEW check and the upgrading mark one atomic step (e.g. a DefaultResponse method that returns true and records 'upgrading' under its monitor only while NEW, with the abort hook consulting it).

findings.title: relay accepts contentLength below -1 silently as an unknown length
findings.description: relay(in, -5) goes through startBody, which treats any negative length as unknown framing without validation.
findings.drop_reason: Relay framing and length validation belong to FR-HTTP-036/037 (later waves), outside the IR-HTTP-014/FR-HTTP-035 guarantee scope.

findings.title: Legacy path still runs middleware when the exchange was already aborted at hook registration
findings.description: A built-in adapter notifies a registration after an abort at once, so the new hook aborts the response before pipeline.run, yet middleware still runs on an ABORTED response.
findings.drop_reason: Not a regression: before 184e89c the legacy path ran middleware on an aborted exchange as well; the hook now ends the response ABORTED (no upgrade, one aborted line via late onDone registration), which is the AC-7 behaviour. No AC requires short-circuiting middleware.

No new issues on append/Vary merge, relay delegation, onAbort registration ordering (state read + AbortListeners), abort() finally ordering, or Java 8/API 21 usage.
